messages:
alicia: Heads-up — we just hit GPU provisioning quota errors in eu-west1-a when autoscaler tried to spin up a mixed pool (reserved + preemptible). Several jobs failed with `quotaExceeded` and CA retried, then timed out. Can infra ops triage? :grimacing:
ben: I saw the alert. repro looks like: autoscaler requested 6 nodes, cloud returned 0 and `quotaExceeded`. warm-pool in the same region had 2 nodes but different taint, so scheduler wouldn't place pods.
carlo: Did CA fall back to another region, or did it keep retrying in the same zone?
alicia: CA kept retrying in eu-west1-a until the request expired. No cross-region spillover because our routing policy requires same-region first. We ended up backlog-queuing pods.
priya: We intentionally prevent cross-region scheduling to avoid data egress, but maybe we need an emergency arbitration path for critical infer endpoints. Suggestion: add a controlled failover policy where only canary routes use cross-region warm pools.
ben: Agree. Also noticed the nodepool autoscaler min/max settings allowed only scaling reserved pool, not preemptible. So mixed-pool request was unsatisfiable.
carlo: Quick config snippet that caused trouble:
```
apiVersion: cluster.k8s.io/v1
kind: NodePool
spec:
  autoscaling:
    minReplicas: 2
    maxReplicas: 8
  taints:
    - key: "dedicated"
      value: "reserved"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
```
Slots in warmpool are `dedicated:preemptible`, so mismatch.
alicia: Logs from CA show: `failed to find node group with sufficient capacity` followed by `scaleUp failed: cloud provider quotaExceeded`.
priya: For short-term mitigation, we can: 1) relax same-region-only rule for high-priority routes, 2) add an emergency autoscaler policy that can borrow from regional warmpools with a billing tag, 3) add a taint-toleration layer to allow transient placement. Thoughts? :thinking:
ben: Option 2 + 3 seem safest: controlled billing tag lets finance track cross-region egress. But toleration might let lower-priority pods sneak into reserved GPUs — need pod priority gating.
carlo: We also need to update the CA scale-up threshold to consider mixed instance pools. Right now it refuses to merge capacity across tainted pools. I'll open a PR to the autoscaler config to treat warmpool as combinable when `allowCrossPool: true` in policy.
alicia: Can we add an emergency runbook? Something like: 1) flip `allowCrossPool` to true for route X, 2) add temporary toleration on deployment, 3) monitor latency and cost, 4) revert after 30m. Keep it simple.
priya: I'll draft the runbook and post in #oncall-playbooks. For the infra change, @carlo can you put a canary behind a feature flag so it only affects ev-proxy and inference-critical pods?
carlo: Yeah, I'll gate it by pod annotation `inference.redwood/failover: "enabled"`. CA rule will check that. I'll send the PR and a test plan.
deploy-bot: infra-deploy started for autoscaler canary (PR #4567) — tracking: https://git.internal/r/4567 :rocket:
oncall-rotation: Noted. I'll be on standby for rollback if latency or cost spikes.
alicia: Thanks all. Priority: get the canary in next 2 hours, draft runbook, and monitor. If quota errors persist after canary, we'll open a support ticket with cloud provider.
ben: Also FYI — cost estimate for cross-region borrow at current rates ~ +18% per-hour for affected requests. Sharing costing table now.
priya: Copy. I'll include cost footnote in runbook and require a manual approve step for >15% cost delta.
carlo: PR posted, test harness shows warmpool spillover placement passes unit checks. Will coordinate canary window with @oncall-rotation.
alicia: Perfect. Follow-ups: update dashboards with a new metric: `gpu.cross_region_failover_count` and alert at >3 in 10m.
priya: Adding dashboard task to me.
ben: If anyone runs into quota errors, post the cloud request ids here; that'll speed up support ticket.
alicia: i'll paste logs as they come in. thanks! :thumbsup:
